title: Pull Lever
summary: A wall stands in front of the hovering aerial manipulator with a lever mounted on its front face: a bar sticking straight out of the wall toward the robot from a small dark-grey base, ending in a horizontal crossbar handle. The lever pivots at the base about a horizontal axis parallel to the wall. Pull the lever up: rotate it so its free end rises by more than 40 degrees from its starting direction, perpendicular to the wall (its travel ends at 45 degrees).
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. Its distance, its sideways offset and a slight tilt (the top leaning toward or away from the robot by up to 5 degrees) vary between instances. On its front face a lever is mounted: a fixed dark-grey base block (15 cm tall, 6 cm wide, standing 6 cm out from the wall) and, pivoting at the base's centre about a horizontal axis parallel to the wall face, a bar 30 cm long, 6 cm tall and 3 cm wide that at reset sticks straight out toward the robot; at its free end is a crossbar handle, a horizontal cylinder about 4 cm in diameter and 15 cm long, parallel to the wall. The bar can swing up or down by at most 45 degrees from perpendicular. It is spring-loaded toward the perpendicular rest position and strongly damped, so it creeps back there when released. The base is dark grey; the bar and the crossbar keep the lever model's own materials (AM-Bench re-colours them at random at every reset, which is switched off here: their colours do not change). The lever's height and sideways position on the wall vary between instances. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration except the wrist roll, which starts turned by 90 degrees (the gripper fingers close vertically and the end-effector camera is rolled by 90 degrees); the end effector is a little ahead of and above the airframe and the gripper is closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = 0 rad and arm_link4_roll_joint = pi/2 rad (this task's FA-Hexa config overrides the wrist roll to 90 degrees); arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m (the roll axis passes through it) with orientation (0.7071, 0.7071, 0, 0) wxyz (rolled +90 degrees about world x: the fingers' closing axis, ee_link y, is world z) and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, nominal centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m and orientation identity (front face the plane x = centre_x - 0.05, normal -x, toward the robot); friction 1.0 static / 1.0 dynamic, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl (loaded from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server). At each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the centre becomes (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently, and the orientation becomes quat_from_euler_xyz(0, pitch, 0) with pitch ~ U(-pi/36, pi/36) rad (a rotation about the world y axis through the wall centre; positive pitch tilts the top of the wall away from the robot, the front normal turning upward). Lever: articulation lever.usd spawned with uniform scale 2.0 (dimensions below are scaled), base body fixed to the world by a fixed joint, self-collisions disabled, solver iterations 8 position / 1 velocity, gravity disabled, masses not authored (PhysX derives them from the collision shapes). At each reset, after the wall, the root (body 'base', at the base centre) is placed at wall_centre + R_wall (-0.08, ly, lz) with ly, lz ~ U(-0.3, 0.3) m independently (0.03 m in front of the wall surface) with orientation R_wall composed with (0.7071, 0, -0.7071, 0) wxyz: for an upright wall the lever's local +x is world +z, local +y world +y, local +z world -x (toward the robot); AM-Bench's lever_pos observation is this root position. Base: box 0.15 (local x) x 0.06 (y) x 0.06 (local z) m centred on the root, its back flush with the wall. Moving body 'lever': bar box 0.06 (local x) x 0.03 (y) x 0.30 m (local z 0 to 0.30 from the pivot) and crossbar cylinder radius 0.0214 m, length 0.15 m, axis along local y, centred at local z = 0.30 (0.33 m in front of the wall surface at reset). Revolute joint lever_joint at the root, axis local +y (world +y for any wall pitch); limits [-45, 45] degrees = [-pi/4, pi/4] rad; positive rotation swings the free end up: at joint angle q the bar points along (-cos(pitch + q), 0, sin(pitch + q)). Reset to 0 rad with zero velocity every episode. Isaac Lab implicit actuator: stiffness 20 N m/rad toward the target 0 rad, damping 100 N m s/rad, effort limit 50 N m, velocity limit 5 rad/s. At every reset Isaac Lab mdp.randomize_visual_color gives the bar and the crossbar each a random RGB colour, every channel ~ U(0.05, 0.95). No physics material on the lever: scene default friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0. Web assets: the lever's vMaterials_2 MDLs (Plastic_Thick_Translucent 'plastic_dark_gray' on the base, Carpaint_Metallic and Plastic_Thick_Translucent on the bar and crossbar) come from NVIDIA's Omniverse content server.
success: Success when the revolute joint lever_joint has position > 40 degrees = 0.698132 rad (lever_pull_angle_min; strict inequality), i.e. the bar's free end is raised more than 40 degrees from the wall normal. The joint ranges from -pi/4 to pi/4 rad and starts at 0 rad every reset; positive is free end up, so pushing the lever down never counts. AM-Bench also reports subtask criteria lever_engaged (joint position >= 0.05 x 0.698132 = 0.034907 rad) and lever_pulled (the success condition); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
difficulty_note: The lever is spring-loaded back to perpendicular and heavily damped, and it has to be driven past 40 degrees, within 5 degrees of its end stop, from a free-flying, hovering base; its place on the wall changes per instance.
standard_notes: The lever's pose and angle are not given: the lever on the concrete wall has to be found with the onboard cameras (its base is dark grey) and related to the robot through proprioception (base and end-effector poses). The lever's angle can only be judged visually. The end-effector camera starts rolled by 90 degrees with the wrist.
